object: Central part of the facade of the Ospedale degli Innocenti, Florence
creator: Filippo Brunelleschi; later alterations and additions by others
work_date: Construction began 1419; Brunelleschi directed works 1419–1427, per Museo degli Innocenti
branch: Florentine Early Renaissance architectural ordering; present-day central facade with later additions
attribution: HuthBerlin, Spedale-degli-innocenti-fassade-01.jpg, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Provider resized preview; no local crop or retouch.
rights_evidence: The exact Commons file description/API identifies HuthBerlin, 28 September 2018 and CC BY 4.0. It describes the central facade of the Ospedale degli Innocenti.
limits: Perspective is near-frontal but slightly upward; do not measure exact module ratios, column-to-span equality or mathematical proportions from pixels. The image does not show the whole facade, full axial symmetry, plan, vault geometry or interior spatial system. Photograph date is 2018; construction began 1419. Do not label the photograph or every visible addition as 1419. Infant tondi are later additions of 1487 according to the museum; they identify this building but are not a necessary Renaissance style criterion. Upper windows, heraldry and frescoes should not all be attributed to Brunelleschi from this photograph. This is an early Florentine architectural example; the gray-and-white palette and round arches alone cannot classify all media as Renaissance or distinguish later Renaissance revival buildings without provenance. A small street bin remains. No local removal, cropping or image generation was used.
retrieval_method: Publicly exposed provider image/thumbnail downloaded unchanged; no access control bypass.
image_transformation: None locally; unchanged public Commons 1280px thumbnail.
observable_features: Near-frontal sequence of five complete semicircular arcade bays, with additional bays cut by the frame edges.
Slender columns and articulated capitals carry the repeated round arches; the shafts, bases and steps remain legible.
Gray pietra serena outlines contrast with broad light plaster fields; the order continues across capitals, arch bands and horizontal courses.
Repeated pedimented upper windows and horizontal cornice courses make the facade organization easy to read.
No parked vehicles, tourists, foreground statue or temporary market covers obstruct the arcade.
